Chronicle
description:
> Chronicle v1.0.0 is built on Inner Self v1.0.2 by LewdLeah, used and modified under the MIT licence, with the original copyright retained in the library script. Auto-Cards is bundled unmodified. Please visit @LewdLeah on AI Dungeon through the link above; none of this exists without that work. ❤️

> Suggested order for a long campaign. Every module in the entry above ships switched off, so turn them on in stages rather than all at once. Turns 1 to 50, add tiered memory and watch /diag. Once the compliance band holds healthy and /diag confirms injections are landing, add the world chronicle, the console, and diagnostics. Add the knowledge model and clocks around turn 100. Add ensemble last, and only at Mythic context or above, because concurrent brains are where format compliance breaks first.

> Modules A, K and L have no switch and always run. A is the transaction ledger that makes retry safe, K scales every injection budget to your live context size, and L watches whether your model can still follow the operation grammar. Turning any of them off would break the rest.

> Type /help in the adventure for the console, once you have enabled it. /diag shows your context profile, compliance band, and what each module is costing you per turn. /state shows the world. /undo reverts the last committed change.

> Avoid the Atlas and Raven models entirely; they cannot receive anything this script injects. Turn Optimized Context off if your model offers it, or the world simulation is silently discarded. Tuned for DeepSeek V3.2, Dynamic DeepSeek, Gemma 31B, and GLM 5.1.

> What each setting on this card does:

> Enable Chronicle: Turns the whole system on or off. Off leaves your cards and memories untouched.

> Show detailed guide: Prints the full player guide into the story once, for you to read and erase.

> First name of player character: Used to keep the story in your character's perspective, and to name who a bond is with.

> Adventure in 1st, 2nd, or 3rd person: Which narrative perspective the prompts ask for.

> Max brain size relative to story context: How much of the recent story budget a character's thoughts may occupy.

> Recent turns searched for name triggers: How far back Chronicle looks for a character name before deciding who thinks.

> Visual indicator of current NPC triggers: Symbol shown beside the card of whoever is thinking. Leave empty to disable.

> Thought formation chance per turn: How often a triggered character is asked to form a thought.

> Half thought chance for Do/Say/Story: Halves that chance on turns you drove, so your own actions stay yours.

> Brain card notes store brains as JSON: Shows thoughts as raw JSON instead of the friendlier key: value form. Both parse.

> Enable debug mode to see model tasks: Leaves the raw operation text inline in the story, for when you are debugging.

> Pin this config card near the top: Keeps this card high in your story card list.

> Install Auto-Cards: Enables the bundled Auto-Cards, which generates story cards as you play.

title:
Configure Chronicle 
· Modules
description:
Chronicle module settings. Each module's detail rows appear in the entry above only while that module is switched on. While it is off, the value documented here applies.

> Tiered memory with pinned core thoughts: Pinned, long-term and working memory tiers. A full brain evicts its coldest working thought instead of asking the model what to burn.

> Maximum pinned core thoughts per character: How many thoughts one character may pin. Pin with /pin, or by putting # in front of a key in their notes.

> Maximum characters of thought per brain: How large a brain may grow before the coldest working thought is evicted.

> Story links before a thought becomes long-term: How many times a thought must surface in the story before eviction can no longer take it.

> Track world state (date, place, arc, factions): Keeps a "Chronicle" card holding the date, location, arc, standing, debts and threats, and injects a short block of it each turn. Edit that card and Chronicle believes you.

> Maximum characters of world state per turn: Ceiling on that block. Whole lines are dropped by priority rather than cut mid sentence.

> In-game date the adventure began on: Where the calendar starts. It moves on narrative phrasing, never once per turn.

> Maximum days one turn may advance: Cap on a single time skip, unless the text carries an explicit [+n days] marker.

> Track who witnessed what, and what they still believe: Characters are told what they missed, and keep acting on facts that changed while they were away.

> Maximum characters of witnessed event log: Byte cap on the record of what happened and who saw it.

> Chance per turn that a secret spreads to someone: Base rate at which an unwitnessed fact reaches someone. Sealed facts never move on their own.

> Enable diagnostics and safety rails: Watches saved state size and hook time, skips optional work rather than risk a timeout, and keeps a "Chronicle Diagnostics" card.

> Milliseconds a hook may spend before skipping extras: Time budget per hook. The platform's own ceiling is two seconds.

> Maximum characters of saved adventure state: Chronicle warns at 60% of this and trims at 85%, dropping the most expendable things first.

> Turns to stop asking after the model cannot answer: The compliance monitor always runs and has no switch. This is how long it waits before trying a model again once it has stopped answering.
